reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every real normed vector space E (with normed additive commutative group structure), equipped with a measurable-space structure in which every norm-open set is measurable, for every measure mu on E of finite total mass, and for every function f from E to the real numbers, the following holds. If f has arbitrarily many continuous real Frechet derivatives, then, for every real number M, if |f(x)| <= M for every x in E and the derivative map x -> Df(x) has compact support, both of the following conclusions hold:
(1) The real-valued function x -> ||Df(x)||^2 is integrable with respect to mu.
(2) For every real e sufficiently close to 0 in the ordinary two-sided real neighborhood filter at 0, including e = 0, all five of the following properties hold simultaneously: (a) 1/2 <= 1 + e*f(x) for every x in E; (b) the function x -> sqrt(1 + e*f(x)) has arbitrarily many continuous real Frechet derivatives; (c) that function belongs to MemLp with exponent 2 with respect to mu; (d) the function x -> (sqrt(1 + e*f(x)))^2 * log((sqrt(1 + e*f(x)))^2) is integrable with respect to mu; and (e) the function x -> ||D(y -> sqrt(1 + e*f(y)))(x)||^2 is integrable with respect to mu.
Here D is the totalized real Frechet derivative, valued in continuous real linear maps, and its norm is the operator norm. Compact support of the derivative map means that the closure of {x in E : Df(x) is nonzero} is compact. The square root is the nonnegative real square root with its stipulated totalized values for negative inputs, and log is the stipulated totalized real logarithm. Integrable includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; MemLp with exponent 2 includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 norm. The measure is assumed finite, not assumed to have total mass one. Smoothness here means arbitrarily many continuous derivatives, not analyticity.
objects: The objects are a real normed vector space E together with the stated additive, normed, real-linear and measurable structures; a finite measure mu on E; a real-valued function f on E; a real pointwise bound M; the real totalized Frechet derivative Df and its operator norm; and the real-parameter family u_e(x) = sqrt(1 + e*f(x)). The logarithmic integrand is exactly u_e(x)^2 * log(u_e(x)^2), and the last derivative is the derivative of the whole function y -> u_e(y).
domains: E is an arbitrary normed real vector space, with no completeness or finite-dimensionality hypothesis. Its measurable-space structure must make all norm-open sets measurable; no equality with the Borel measurable structure is required. mu ranges over finite measures on E, not only probability measures. f, u_e and the integrands take real values. x and y range over E; M and e range over all real numbers. The derivatives are continuous real-linear maps from E to the real numbers with operator norm. The MemLp exponent is 2.
quantifiers: The order is: for every E with the specified structures, every finite mu, and every f, assume f is smooth; then for every real M, assume the bound at every x, and assume compact support of the derivative map. The conclusion is the conjunction of unconditional-in-e integrability of ||Df||^2 and an eventual statement in e at 0. Inside that one eventual statement, all five properties are conjoined. Only the lower-bound property has an additional explicit pointwise quantifier, for every x in E; the other four concern entire functions on E. The eventual statement means that some real neighborhood of 0 works for every e in it, so it covers both signs and zero.
assumptions: The premises are the normed additive commutative group and real normed-space structures on E, a measurable-space structure with every norm-open set measurable, finite total mass of mu, genuine ContDiff real infinity smoothness of f, the global pointwise bound |f(x)| <= M, and compact support of the derivative map. Compact support is compactness of the closure of its nonzero set, not compactness of E and not compact support of f. There is no separate sign restriction on M or e and no assumption that mu is normalized. The infinity smoothness order is not an analytic-order hypothesis.
conclusion: First, x -> ||Df(x)||^2 is integrable with respect to mu. Second, eventually for e in the ordinary neighborhood filter of 0, the following all hold together: the pointwise bound 1/2 <= 1 + e*f(x) for every x; smoothness of u_e; membership of u_e in MemLp at exponent 2; integrability of x -> u_e(x)^2 * log(u_e(x)^2); and integrability of x -> ||D u_e(x)||^2. Each Integrable assertion includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite norm integral, and MemLp includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 norm. No value of an integral or additional limiting assertion is concluded.
scopes: All conclusions remain under every stated premise and every chosen E, mu, f and M. The integrability assertion for the original derivative is outside the eventual-e scope. A single eventual-e scope encloses the conjunction of all five perturbed-function properties; there is no separate almost-everywhere quantification over e. The domain-wide bound is pointwise for every x, not merely mu-almost everywhere. The compact-support condition concerns x -> Df(x). Each perturbed derivative differentiates in the E-variable y, with e fixed, and is then evaluated at x. The filter is the full two-sided neighborhood filter at zero, not a punctured or one-sided filter and not a convergence assertion.
constant_dependencies: M is a universally quantified real bound under the preceding choices, not an existentially supplied constant and not an additional fixed universal constant. The numerical threshold 1/2 and exponent 2 are fixed as displayed. The neighborhood of e = 0 is permitted to depend on the preceding quantified data E and its structures, mu, f and M under the hypotheses; the statement supplies no explicit radius, rate or uniform neighborhood over different choices. It asserts no further constants or dependence claims.
